task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: Does the magnitude of reorganization predict the change in PPP across absence spells?
Is the reorganization measure defined independently of the PPP outcome, and is it reliable at spell-level possession counts?
Is 148 spells enough power to detect a plausible correlation?
How can regression to the mean, selection of absences and confounding by absentee quality and opponent be controlled?

historical_evidence.finding: Absence validation. Real absences moved the association structure (V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95; V1(b) mean +0.142, CI [+0.103,+0.187]; recorded as confirmed in [prior work]). The magnitude-prediction step (V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244,+0.667]; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115) failed. [prior work] cites [prior work].

Live trigger timing study: Spearman tier vs outcome rho was -0.2066 (n=557) in one sub-result and -0.0457 (p=0.456, n=268) in another. These are different units and constructs, so [prior work] is only loosely related to this question.
Player routing V4 vs V5: 0 of 8 divergences were scoreable. [prior work] gives the failure mechanism as A_unanswerable and lists RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER and RISK:DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY.
An apparent PPP [source] of about +1.13 to +1.26 came from small-sample inflation (e.g. 6 possessions at 3.00 PPP). [prior work] gives the failure mechanism as C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of absence-driven structural change (V2a/V2b) from a leave-one-out simulation across 23 real absences
failed_approaches.why: The CIs span zero and [prior work] cites [prior work]. Structure moving under absence was confirmed, but magnitude prediction was not.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Scoring routing choices by observed PPP on sparse divergences
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: 0 of 8 scoreable, with small_sample and drift risks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading PPP differences from low-possession leaders
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the [source] came from small-sample inflation.

evidence_establishes: Per FAM:[prior work] (V1), real absences measurably move the association structure of the offense beyond a null, so there is something to measure.
Per FAM:[prior work] (V2), an earlier attempt to predict the magnitude of that movement was not significant at n=23 (rho about +0.25 to +0.29, wide CI), with the point estimates positive.
Per FAM:[prior work] and [prior work][prior work], PPP computed on few possessions is unstable and has produced artifacts and unscoreable tests.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether reorganization magnitude predicts the change in PPP. No retrieved record tests this directly.
Whether the earlier magnitude result (n=23) would hold or vanish at n=148 spells.
What 'L' denotes in this project. No retrieved record defines it, and its definition decides the leakage and mechanical-link risks.
Any causal effect of reorganization on efficiency.
own_inferences: The directional prior is weakly positive but small. The [prior work] rho of about 0.25 to 0.29 had a very wide CI, and it is a different outcome than PPP.
With n=148 the minimum detectable |rho| is about 0.23 at 80% power and two-sided alpha 0.05. A true effect near 0.1 to 0.2 would probably be missed, so a null would not be strongly informative.

The sign of the PPP change is ambiguous. Large reorganization might reflect successful adaptation or a team that has lost its main creator. A one-sided hypothesis could fail for reasons unrelated to the mechanism.
Absentee quality (usage and value) likely drives both reorganization size and PPP change. This confounder would inflate any raw correlation.
If the reorganization measure uses points, shot results or play-type PPP, a mechanical link to PPP change is likely and the result could be an artifact.
uncertainties: The definition of L (baseline lineup, league, or a leave-one-out simulation) is not given.
The spell definition, minimum possessions per spell and overlap between spells are unknown. n=986 against 148 spells is unexplained.
The reliability of the reorganization metric at spell-level possession counts is unknown.
[prior work] retrieved are only tangential, and I did not open the full [prior work] record.

historical_effect.explanation: [prior work] moved the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes. [prior work] shows that magnitude-prediction at small n gave wide, non-significant intervals, and [prior work] and SF-[prior work] show small-possession PPP producing artifacts and unscoreable tests. So I require a possession floor, an outcome-independent reorganization measure and shrinkage. I also frame the result as an estimate with a CI rather than a pass/fail, since the null is likely to be underpowered.

blocking_constraints.text: 148 spells give an MDE of rho about 0.23, which is above the likely true effect. A null result would be uninformative.
If the reorganization metric is built from play-type points or efficiency, or L is outcome-derived, the link to PPP change is mechanical. The metric must be defined without outcome fields.

prior_work.summary: [prior work] confirmed that absences move offensive structure but did not confirm that its magnitude is predicted (n=23, not significant). No retrieved record tests reorganization magnitude against PPP change. [prior work] and SF-[prior work] warn about small-possession PPP.

risks.text: 148 spells give MDE rho about 0.23. The [prior work] analogue (n=23) was significant on neither V2 test.
Spell-level reorganization and PPP are computed on limited possessions, so noise attenuates the correlation. [prior work] shows how small-n PPP inflates.
If reorganization or L uses points or play-type PPP, the correlation with PPP change is built in.
Larger absences (higher usage) mechanically force larger shifts in the play-type mix and also lower PPP, so some association exists without any causal effect of reorganization.
Absentee quality, replacement quality, opponent defense, game state, home/away and season all affect both reorganization and PPP.
If spells are selected on unusually high or low baseline PPP, or on unusual absences, the PPP change regresses toward the mean.
If L is estimated using post-absence games or the same possessions that define the outcome, the baseline leaks information.
Four seasons with rule, pace and league play-style changes make league-level baselines drift. Spells may also cluster within teams.
Several reorganization metrics, PPP definitions or subgroup splits would inflate false positives unless fixed in advance.

design.estimand: Spearman rho, and an adjusted partial slope, between spell-level reorganization magnitude R (distance between the on-court play-type/initiator distribution during the absence and baseline L) and the change in PPP (absence minus baseline). The PPP change is shrunk toward the team mean. R is defined without any points or result fields.
design.unit: One team-absence spell: a contiguous set of games or possessions without a specified key player, paired with that team's baseline L.
design.sample: Spells from 2022-23 to 2025-26, regular season and playoffs, with data frozen at the analysis date. The 148 spells are the maximum; the rule requiring at least 100 possessions in both the absence and baseline windows is set before looking at outcomes, and drops are reported. Baseline L comes only from games before the spell, or from a leave-one-out on the same team-season excluding the absence. Overlapping spells are merged.
design.power: With n=148 and rho=0.25, power is about 0.85 at alpha 0.05 two-sided. The MDE is about 0.23 for 80% power. A true rho of 0.15 would have power of about 0.35, so a null is reported as an equivalence-style CI, not as evidence of no effect. Adding season-split replication is not possible at this n, so one pooled test is run.
design.controls: Cluster-robust (team) standard errors or a mixed model with team-season random effect. Covariates: absentee usage or on-off value, replacement quality, minutes, opponent defensive rating, home/away, game-state/garbage-time exclusion, season. Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of PPP change to handle RTM. Separate sensitivity analyses with and without the largest-usage absences.
design.falsification: (1) Permutation placebo: assign each spell a random non-absence window from the same team-season and compute R and the PPP change. Real rho must exceed the placebo distribution (p95). (2) Negative control: R computed on a role player's absence with minimal usage. (3) Verify R has no mechanical relation to PPP by recomputing it with PPP-neutral features. (4) Partial out absentee usage; if rho drops to about 0, the result is classed as mechanical.
design.multiplicity: One primary test with a single pre-specified R and a single PPP definition. All alternative metrics or subgroups are exploratory and reported with Holm correction over the stated family.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary rho is at least 0.20, the 95% cluster-bootstrap CI excludes 0, it survives the usage-adjusted partial and exceeds the placebo p95. Rejected if the 95% CI lies within [-0.15, 0.15]. Artifact if the raw rho is significant but the adjusted partial or placebo fails. Otherwise inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and the derived play-type graph for 2022-23 through 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs), frozen as of the 2026-11-01 data cut. Record the snapshot hash, the code commit and the definition of L before the analysis.
